decisions.reason: The anamnesis and consent app is the firm's flagship product line and sits close to its core offer, and post-2020 demand for digital, contactless practice workflows likely pushed its results above aspiration, so there is no trigger for search.

The education institute reuses existing training content and customer relationships at low cost, and in a growing firm with slack, any pandemic-related dip in attendance can be absorbed through online formats rather than withdrawal.

The analytics dashboard extends the core practice software with data the firm already holds and fits its connected-practice direction, so even with uncertain results the firm's slack lets it keep developing the module.
The complete practice bundle mainly repackages core modules for new and growing practices at little extra cost, so there is no performance shortfall that would justify dropping it.

The listing portal is distant from the core offer and faces strong specialised competitors, so it is the most likely candidate for problemistic search, but its low upkeep and the firm's growth-based slack make keeping it for another year the satisficing choice.
